facts.statement: The genus contains a single species named Austroposeidon magnificus, which means "Magnificent Southern Poseidon".
facts.quote: It contains one species, Austroposeidon magnificus (meaning "Magnificent Southern Poseidon").

facts.statement: The specimen was discovered in 1953 by Llewellyn Ivor Price in the Presidente Prudente Formation but was not formally described until 2016.
facts.quote: The specimen was discovered in the Campanian-Maastrichtian Presidente Prudente Formation of the Bauru Group by palaeontologist Llewellyn Ivor Price in an outcrop along the Raposo Tavares Road in 1953, but the remains were not described until 2016.

facts.statement: The original fossil site has been lost to urban development and could not be located by researchers.
facts.quote: Unfortunately, the site where the specimen was recovered has now been lost to urban development after Felipe Medeiros Simbras was unable to locate the site.

facts.statement: The genus name combines "austro" for South America and "Poseidon," the Greek god of earthquakes.
facts.quote: The genus name combines austro ("southern", as in South America, from Latin Auster, the southern wind) and poseidon, a reference to the Greek god of earthquakes of the same name.

facts.statement: The species name "magnificus" refers to the large size of the known specimen.
facts.quote: The specific name is the Latin word magnificus ("great, elevated, noble"), referring to the large size of the specimen.

facts.statement: Austroposeidon is the largest dinosaur discovered in Brazil, with the single known adult specimen reaching about 25 meters in length.
facts.quote: Austroposeidon was a large sauropod, the largest dinosaur discovered in Brazil, with the only known specimen, an adult, having a length of about 25 m.

facts.statement: Austroposeidon is identified as a titanosaur by missing hyposphene-hypantrum articulations, non-forked neural spines, and camellate bone texture with air chambers.
facts.quote: Several traits show that Austroposeidon was a titanosaur; the hyposphene-hypantrum articulations are missing from the vertebrae, the cervical and dorsal vertebrae do not have forked neural spines, and the internal texture of the bone is camellate (punctuated by many small air chambers).

facts.statement: CT scans revealed concentric alternating rings of camellate and dense tissue in the vertebrae, interpreted by researchers as growth rings.
facts.quote: A CT scan showed that the internal bone texture of the vertebrae possessed concentric, alternating rings of camellate tissue and dense tissue; the describers interpreted these as rings of growth within the bone.

facts.statement: A 2016 phylogenetic analysis recovered Austroposeidon as the sister taxon to the group Lognkosauria.
facts.quote: A phylogenetic analysis in 2016 recovered Austroposeidon as the sister taxon of the Lognkosauria.

facts.statement: A 2022 study by Navarro et al. recovered Austroposeidon as a member of the group Lognkosauria.
facts.quote: In 2022, Austroposeidon was recovered as a member of Lognkosauria by Navarro et al.

facts.statement: Austroposeidon magnificus lived between 83.6 and 66 million years ago during the Campanian stage of the Late Cretaceous in South America.
facts.quote: Austroposeidon magnificus ("Poseidón del sur magnífico") es la única especie conocida del género extinto Austroposeidon de dinosaurio saurópodo titanosaurio que vivió entre 83.6 a 66 millones de años durante el Campaniano en el Cretácico Superior de Sudamérica.

facts.statement: The only known adult specimen of Austroposeidon was about 25 meters (82 feet) long, making it the largest known dinosaur in Brazil.
facts.quote: Austroposeidon era un saurópodo grande: el único espécimen conocido, que era adulto, tendría una longitud de cerca de 25 metros (82 pies); de hecho, es el dinosaurio más grande conocido de Brasil a la fecha.

facts.statement: Researchers established Austroposeidon as a new genus based on unique vertebral traits, including columnar laminae on the thirteenth cervical vertebra, split posterior laminae, curved first dorsal laminae, and forked frontmost laminae in dorsal vertebrae.
facts.quote: Los descriptores determinaron que Austroposeidon constituye un nuevo género basándose en ciertas autapomorfias (o características únicas de los fósiles en cuestión) en las vértebras: la decimotercera vértebra cervical tiene láminas columnares centropostzigapofisiales, y la lámina posterior centrodiapofisial se divide en dos proyecciones; la primera vértebra dorsal tiene láminas centrodiapofisiales posteriores y anteriores que se curvan hacia abajo y hacia afuera, y su diapófisis se estrecha hasta el margen superior del centro de la vértebra; y la parte más frontal de la lámina espinoprezigapofisial se bifurca en las vértebras dorsales posicionadas hacia la parte posterior del torso.

facts.statement: A 2016 phylogenetic analysis found Austroposeidon to be the sister taxon of the Lognkosauria group.
facts.quote: Un análisis filogenético presentado con la descripción del fósil de 2016 encontró que Austroposeidon es el taxón hermano del grupo Lognkosauria.

facts.statement: Austroposeidon lived from the Campanian to the Maastrichtian, spanning 83.6 to 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Maastrichtian (83.6 to 66 million years ago)
